primary.title: Integration of polygenic risk with single cell methylation data using met-scDRS.
primary.abstract: MOTIVATION: Although large scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified many risk variants for psychiatric traits their functional implication remain largely unknown. One potential mechanism for their risk is through cellular context-dependent epigenetics such as methylation. Previous methodologies have focused on integrating GWAS with single cell transcriptomics, which allowed identification of within-cell-type heterogeneity in disease risk association. We extended this framework to provide a method called met-scDRS that integrates GWAS with single cell epigenomics and investigates how psychiatric disease risk can manifest through methylomics at single cell resolution. RESULTS: We propose an approach that integrates single cell methylomes with disease associated genes identified from GWAS at single-cell resolution. We found our method to be well calibrated and powered in different scenarios. We then analyzed a publicly available single cell methylome dataset of the human brain for 75 different traits and generated disease relevance scores for each cell for each trait. We find high brain specificity with major cell type enrichments congruent with known findings. We identify within-cell-type heterogeneity for psychiatric disease risk along the brain spatial axis as well as subpopulations that are differentially associated with diseases. Finally, we showed that genes with high correlation between methylation levels and disease relevance scores to be highly enriched in specific functional pathways such as synaptic formation and transmission. AVAILABILITY: met-scDRS is freely available in GitHub as a python package under MIT license: https://github.com/bogdanlab/met-scDRS. Source code is also available from Zenodo with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21841506. All dataset used in this work are publicly available. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

primary.overview: MOTIVATION: Although large scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified many risk variants for psychiatric traits their functional implication remain largely unknown.
primary.main: RESULTS: We propose an approach that integrates single cell methylomes with disease associated genes identified from GWAS at single-cell resolution.

primary.title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics uncovers region-specific molecular features underlying selective aging vulnerability of cholinergic neurons.
primary.abstract: Cholinergic neurons exhibit functional and molecular heterogeneity across the basal forebrain (BF), midbrain (MB), and brainstem (BS), while the aging-associated transcriptional features remain poorly characterized. Here, we performed single nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on 108,062 nuclei from the MS/VDB, HDB/SI, PPTG/LDTG, 7N, and 12N in adult and aged mice. BF cells showed greater age-associated transcriptomic alterations than MB and BS cells, with pronounced region-specific divergence among cholinergic neurons. Intercellular communication analysis revealed BF-specific age-related changes in APP and ApoE signaling. Within this altered milieu, intrinsic transcriptional responses varied across brain regions. In aged BF cholinergic neurons, transcriptional responses were characterized by increased oxidative stress and inflammatory signatures and reduced expression of genes involved in neuronal structural maintenance. In contrast, MB and BS cholinergic neurons maintained relatively stable transcriptional profiles. These findings reveal region-specific associations between extracellular signaling and intrinsic transcriptional stress, highlighting a selective imbalance that underlies the vulnerability of BF cholinergic neurons.

primary.title: Female iPSC X chromosome inactivation erosion and its transcriptomic effects during CRISPR gene editing and neural differentiation.
primary.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), together with CRISPR editing, are commonly used for studying neurodevelopmental disorders. Female iPSCs gradually lose the expression of the noncoding X chromosome inactive-specific transcript (XIST), leading to random X chromosome inactivation (XCI) erosion that affects both X-linked and autosomal gene expression. However, the effects of CRISPR editing and neural differentiation on XCI erosion and how this may confound a real-world analysis of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) are poorly understood. Here, we analyzed hundreds of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) samples of CRISPR-edited iPSC lines for 66 genes and the matched single-neuron RNA-seq data. We found variable XCI in CRISPR-edited female iPSCs, which was largely preserved in iPSC-derived neurons and predominantly influenced X-linked genes. Mechanistically, XIST mediates allele-specific epigenetic regulation of both X-linked and autosomal genes, with the former showing stronger allele-specific expression (ASE) bias that affects neurodevelopmental genes. These results have significant implications in hiPSC-based modeling of neurodevelopmental disorders.

primary.title: Single-cell atlas of neuroma-induced DRG remodeling reveals intervention-specific glial and immune programs.
primary.abstract: Peripheral nerve injury caused by cut, crush, or excessive stretch can lead to disordered regeneration and painful neuroma formation. Regrowing axons may terminate in a swollen, hypersensitive nerve stump, producing pain that can outweigh sensory or motor deficits. Despite the frequency of neuromas, treatment outcomes remain inconsistent, and the mechanisms that initiate and sustain neuroma-associated pain are poorly understood. A proximal nerve crush performed upstream of a neuroma or transection may reshape axonal growth and interrupt retrograde injury signaling, potentially promoting a regenerative, pain-resolving state. However, its long-term effects on dorsal root ganglion (DRG) programs remain unclear. Here, we use single-cell RNA sequencing to build an atlas of DRG remodeling after neuroma-forming injury and compare it with two interventions: proximal nerve crush and nerve resection. By resolving transcriptional responses across sensory neurons, satellite glial cells, Schwann cells, and macrophages, we identify intervention-specific glial, neuronal, and immune programs that distinguish regenerative from persistent injury-associated states and nominate pathways that may guide mechanism-based therapies for painful neuromas.

primary.title: An integrative transcriptomic atlas of ALS and aging skeletal muscle defines shared and distinct molecular programs of degeneration.
primary.abstract: Skeletal muscle atrophy and weakness resulting from loss of motor neuron innervation are shared hallmarks of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and age-associated sarcopenia. However, muscle wasting in ALS is rapid and severe, whereas sarcopenia progresses gradually over decades, peaking at an advanced age. The molecular mechanisms underlying muscle wasting in these conditions remain incompletely defined. Here, we used the SOD1G93A ALS mouse model and wild-type mice across the lifespan to generate an integrated single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of skeletal muscle, mapping changes associated with ALS and aging. This atlas is complemented by structural and functional analyses. Our results identify transcriptionally distinct condition-specific myonuclear states, including disease-responsive programs within synaptic myonuclei at the neuromuscular junction, that are shared or distinct between the two conditions. Notably, at early stages, muscle from ALS mice exhibits molecular hallmarks of aged muscle at the myofiber level, indicating premature aging and reinforcing aging as a risk factor in ALS. At advanced disease stages and in old age, myonuclear subpopulations follow similar degenerative pathways in fast glycolytic fibers, consistent with their loss in both conditions. However, a distinct ALS-enriched myonuclei subpopulation displays uniquely regulated genes not observed in aged muscle, potentially underlying the more rapid and severe pathology observed in ALS. This atlas maps shared and divergent mechanisms of muscle degeneration in ALS and sarcopenia and provides a resource for identifying therapeutic targets tailored to each condition.

primary.title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen reveals that Wnt signaling regulates lipid accumulation in APOE4 oligodendrocytes.
primary.abstract: APOE4 is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease, yet the cellular mechanisms linking APOE variants to disease risk remain unclear. We previously found that APOE4 expression causes lipid droplet accumulation in oligodendrocytes, reducing myelination, but the underlying mechanisms were unknown. Using a genome-wide CRISPR screen and assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (ATAC) sequencing in human-induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived oligodendrocytes, we identified decreased Wnt signaling and overactive glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK3B) as key regulators of lipid-droplet accumulation. Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of GSK3B reduced lipid droplets in APOE4 oligodendrocytes and increased myelination in three-dimensional iPSC-derived brain organoids. Pharmacological GSK3B inhibition also reduced lipid droplets and improved myelination in APOE4;PS19 tau transgenic mice. Together, these findings establish a mechanistic framework linking Wnt/GSK3B signaling to APOE4-driven disruptions in oligodendrocyte lipid metabolism and myelination, pointing to GSK3B as a potential therapeutic target for APOE4-associated Alzheimer's disease.

primary.title: Multi-omic profiling of 85 iPSC lines from familial dementia reveals cellular diversity and regulators of organoid development.
primary.abstract: Systematic molecular characterization of human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines carrying disease-associated mutations is needed to distinguish disease-related biology from variation in cell state, genomic integrity, and genome-editing history, yet such systematic characterization is uncommon. Here, we profiled 85 human iPSC lines carrying MAPT mutations and isogenic controls using whole-genome sequencing, long-read sequencing of the MAPT locus, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, and DNA methylation arrays. Single-cell analyses identified four reproducible iPSC states and candidate surface markers for their isolation. Whole-genome sequencing revealed unintended editing events and recurrent 20q11.21 duplications, which were associated with increased ID1 expression and impaired cortical organoid patterning. Transcriptomic analyses identified pathways associated with organoid quality and changes linked to clonal selection and editing, underscoring the need to use unconverted lines as isogenic controls. By providing an in-depth genomic characterization of MAPT iPSCs, this dataset serves as a proof of principle to enhance iPSC utility in biological research.

primary.title: Early lineage divergence segregates sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus.
primary.abstract: The thalamus integrates sensory, motor and associative functions through distinct nuclei, yet the developmental principles driving their specification remain unclear. Here we generate a spatiotemporal single-cell multiomic and spatial transcriptomic atlas of the embryonic mouse thalamus, combined with barcoding-based lineage tracing. We identify two major glutamatergic lineages, sensory-related and motor-associative, each governed by different gene regulatory programs and temporal dynamics. These lineages arise from spatially and molecularly distinct progenitor domains, revealing an early segregation of functional identities. Within the sensory lineage, we resolve branching sensory trajectories leading to first-order visual and somatosensory neurons, both emerging from a shared higher-order-like state. Using in silico predictions and in vivo perturbation, we identify Sp9 as a key regulator of visual thalamic fate. Together, our findings define the molecular architecture and developmental trajectories that underpin thalamic modality specification, providing a framework to understand how functional circuits emerge in the mammalian brain.

primary.title: A pathogenic AMPAR mutation disrupts hippocampal synapse maturation and homeostasis.
primary.abstract: AMPA receptors (AMPARs) mediate fast excitatory synaptic transmission and are critical for activity-dependent synapse maturation and circuit development. De novo missense mutations in AMPAR subunits are linked to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), yet how these variants disrupt neuronal function remains unclear. Here, we examine a recurrent pathogenic mutation in the GluA1 subunit (GRIA1 p.A636T) that alters AMPAR function and is associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID). Using GluA1A636T knock-in mice of either sex, we identify impairments in hippocampal-dependent learning and working memory. Quantitative proteomics combined with bulk RNA-seq revealed age-dependent molecular remodeling in mutant hippocampus. Synaptic protein alterations were present in juvenile and adult mice, whereas a pronounced upregulation of mitochondrial and glial-associated proteins emerged more strongly in adulthood. Transcriptomic analyses showed partial concordance and highlighted divergence between RNA and protein regulation. Consistent with these molecular changes, there were increases in markers of oxidative stress in juvenile and adult mutant animals, whereas altered mitochondria morphology emerged selectively in adult mutants. Electrophysiological recordings demonstrated reduced basal excitatory transmission, persistence of silent synapses in adulthood and exaggerated activity-dependent synaptic potentiation, which were associated with reduced spine size consistent with impaired synapse maturation. Together, these findings indicate that a pathogenic AMPAR mutation disrupts developmental synapse maturation with secondary metabolic adaptations emerging over time.Significance Statement Mutations in genes encoding AMPA-type glutamate receptors are increasingly linked to neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism and intellectual disability. However, how these mutations disrupt brain function and development remains poorly understood. Using a mouse model carrying a recurrent disease-associated mutation in the GluA1 AMPA receptor subunit, we show that the presence of this mutant subunit protein impairs the normal maturation of excitatory synapses in the hippocampus. Mutant mice retain immature "silent" synapses into adulthood, exhibit abnormal synaptic plasticity, reduced spine size, and deficits in learning and memory. Molecular analyses reveal age-dependent remodeling of synaptic and mitochondrial proteins, suggesting that metabolic changes arise secondary to disrupted synapse development. These findings clarify how pathogenic AMPA receptor variants alter brain function over time.

primary.title: Identification of Succinylation-Related Transcriptional Signatures in Alzheimer's Disease: Integrated Bioinformatics Analysis and Clinical Validation.
primary.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder involving mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, proteostasis imbalance, and immune-inflammatory alterations. Protein succinylation is closely linked to mitochondrial metabolic status, but peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures related to succinylation in AD remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to identify peripheral blood transcriptional candidate biomarkers associated with a predefined succinylation-related gene set in AD. The GSE63061 dataset was used as the discovery cohort, and GSE63060 served as an external validation cohort. Differential expression analysis, ssGSEA-derived succinylation scoring, and WGCNA were integrated with a predefined succinylation-related gene set. Candidate biomarkers were then refined through four feature selection approaches: LASSO, random forest, SVM-RFE, and Boruta, and their discriminatory performance was evaluated by ROC analysis, nomogram construction, calibration analysis, decision curve analysis, and SHAP analysis. Functional enrichment, GSVA/GSEA, GeneMANIA, immune-cell signature analysis, and single-cell analyses were used to explore biological relevance and cellular distribution. qRT-PCR was performed using peripheral blood-derived PBMC samples for experimental validation. Five genes, NDUFA1, NDUFS5, RPS27A, AIF1, and PRDX1, were identified as candidate biomarkers associated with a succinylation-related transcriptional signature in AD. These genes were mainly involved in mitochondrial complex I activity, oxidative phosphorylation, ribosomal function, protein homeostasis, redox balance, and immune inflammation. Immune-cell signatures and single-cell analyses further suggested that the signature was associated with T cells, B cells, NK cells, and monocytes/macrophages. qRT-PCR confirmed significant downregulation of all five genes in AD PBMC samples (P < 0.05). These findings suggest that peripheral blood transcriptional signatures associated with succinylation-related genes may provide candidate biomarkers and hypothesis-generating clues for AD.

primary.title: FOXG1 spatiotemporally orchestrates subtype fate specification and patch/matrix identity of striatal spiny projection neurons.
primary.abstract: The striatum consists of three main spiny projection neuron subtypes, direct-pathway neurons (dSPNs), indirect-pathway neurons (iSPNs), and recently identified eccentric striatal neurons (eSPNs) with these SPNs organized into two complementary compartments, the patch and the matrix. However, the cellular basis underlying subtype specification especially that of eSPNs, and mechanisms governing the complementary patterning remain unclear. Here, employing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) combined with loss-of-function we reveal that eSPNs share more developmental similarities with iSPNs and the transcription factor Foxg1 promotes dSPN and iSPN fates but suppresses eSPN fate in ventral region of the lateral ganglionic eminence lineage. Deletion of Foxg1 in progenitors forces both dSPNs and iSPNs into an eSPN fate. While postmitotic Foxg1 deletion impairs patch/matrix identity and leads to SPN aggregation. We identify FOXG1-driven transcriptional programs and key transcription factors that specify each striatal SPN subtype and patch/matrix identity, and uncover FOXG1 directly regulated cell migration- and cell adhesion-related molecules that control SPN migration. Our findings provide insights into striatal development.

primary.title: De novo variants in the essential splicing factor gene SRSF3 cause variable developmental phenotypes.
primary.abstract: SRSF3 (SRp20), a member of the serine/arginine-rich protein family of splicing factors, plays a central role in constitutive and alternative splicing. The C-terminal arginine/serine-rich domain of SRSF3 undergoes dynamic phosphorylation cycles that regulate its subcellular localization, protein-protein interactions, and nuclear mRNA export while also indirectly modulating the RNA-binding capability. We report nine individuals with variable developmental phenotypes, including developmental delay and/or mild to moderate intellectual disability as the most consistent feature, and de novo SRSF3 variants. These variants comprise c.181G>C (p.Asp61His) and c.242C>G (p.Ser81Trp), affecting highly conserved residues within the RNA recognition motif, c.330_331del (p.Pro111Serfs∗20), c.402_403del (p.Arg137Ilefs∗16), c.477dup (p.Ser160Valfs∗3), and a recurrent nonsense variant c.445C>T (p.Arg149∗). For c.330_331del, nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) was predicted. Qualitative RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) of fibroblasts from this individual demonstrated NMD of SRSF3 transcripts containing the variant. However, overall SRSF3 mRNA and protein levels were comparable to control cells, suggestive of a compensatory mechanism acting in these cells. Comprehensive functional studies of ectopically expressed SRSF3Asp61His, SRSF3Ser81Trp, SRSF3Arg137Ilefs∗16, SRSF3Arg149∗, and SRSF3Ser160Valfs∗3 in HEK293T cells revealed reduced complex formation with polyadenylated RNA as well as intrinsic instability of C-terminally truncated variant proteins, correlating with decreased C-terminal phosphorylation. Complex formation with the nuclear export proteins YTHDC1 and NXF1 was reduced for SRSF3Arg137Ilefs∗16 and SRSF3Arg149∗ and increased for SRSF3Ser81Trp. Additionally, nucleocytoplasmic shuttling, assessed in HeLa cells, was reduced for the C-terminally truncated SRSF3 variant proteins. Together, our data demonstrate distinct functional defects for the disease-associated SRSF3 variants, which may underlie phenotypic variability in affected individuals.

primary.title: Parkinson's disease-linked D620N mutation selectively alters the brain-specific protein interactome of VPS35.
primary.abstract: Mutations in several genes are known to cause familial forms of Parkinson's disease (PD), including mutations in the vacuolar protein sorting 35 ortholog (VPS35) gene linked to late-onset, autosomal dominant PD. VPS35 encodes a core subunit of the retromer complex which functions in endosomal sorting and recycling. It remains unclear how the pathogenic D620N mutation in VPS35 disrupts retromer function to induce neurodegeneration in PD. Using cell- and rodent-based models expressing D620N VPS35, we performed interactome proteomics to identify alterations underlying the pathogenic effects of D620N VPS35 in PD. Using overexpression of VPS35 variants in HEK-293 T cells, we conducted tandem affinity purification (TAP) or co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) with protein chemical crosslinking to determine the native and non-native protein interactomes of wild-type (WT) and D620N VPS35, respectively. Notably, we can confirm the reduced interaction of D620N VPS35 with components of the WASH complex. Additionally, using a viral-mediated gene transfer model of human D620N VPS35 overexpression in adult rat brain, we identify the first brain-specific protein interactome of VPS35. These overexpression models reveal remarkably similar interaction profiles of WT and D620N VPS35, suggesting that the D620N mutation has a subtle effect on the overall VPS35 protein interactome. We also conducted proteomic analysis of brain tissue from a D620N VPS35 knockin (KI) mouse model that expresses VPS35 at endogenous levels. Using co-IP from hemibrain or striatal extracts of WT and D620N VPS35 KI mice, we reveal a high degree of similarity between the brain interactomes of WT and D620N VPS35, further suggesting a subtle effect of the D620N mutation on VPS35 protein interactions. Notably, in both hemibrain and striatum, we find a selective decrease in the interaction of two known interactors, TBC1D5 and VPS29, with D620N VPS35. We also performed global proteomic analysis of striatal tissue from D620N VPS35 KI mice and reveal a high degree of similarity between WT and D620N, further suggesting a subtle effect of this mutation. Together, our study provides a comprehensive evaluation of the VPS35 protein interactome and reveals a selective effect of the PD-linked D620N mutation in mammalian cells and brain. Our study provides key insight into the mechanisms of retromer dysfunction in VPS35-linked PD.

primary.title: Single-cell multiome landscape reveals elovanoid-mediated suppression of inflammatory glial states and induction of homeostatic signaling after ischemic stroke.
primary.abstract: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of death and disability. Administration of the lipid mediators elovanoids (ELVs) is protective in human neuronal-glia cultures and in experimental ischemic stroke. We now report using a single-cell multiome approach that intranasally-delivered (IN) ELV34 or its precursor reduced the loss of neuronal markers and upregulated homeostatic microglia signatures after stroke. Thus, ELV reduces disease-associated microglia (expressing Spp1, Gpnmb, Lgals3, Clec7a) and the expression of neuroinflammatory signaling genes. In astrocytes, ELV decreased reactive astrocytes (expressing Gfap, Vim, Nes, Lcn2) and upregulated genes involved in synaptic organization. Also, ELV reduced abundance of oligodendrocytes and OPCs expressing immune markers. ELV induced a phenotype shift from pro-inflammatory microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and OPCs in response to ischemic stroke damage. ELV upregulated gene pathways promoting synaptic integrity, reducing immune cell activation and neuronal loss.

primary.title: Patch-seq analysis reveals transcriptomic correlates of neuronal firing rate adaptation across subtypes and species.
primary.abstract: Can the transcriptomic profile of a neuron predict its physiological properties? Using a Patch-seq dataset of the primary visual cortex, we addressed this question by focusing on spike rate adaptation (SRA), a well-known phenomenon that depends on small conductance calcium (Ca)-dependent potassium (SK) channels. We first show that in parvalbumin-expressing (PV) and somatostatin-expressing (SST) interneurons, expression levels of genes encoding the ion channels underlying action potential generation are correlated with the half-width (HW) of spikes. Surprisingly, the SK encoding genes are not correlated with the degree of SRA (dAdap). Instead, genes that encode proteins upstream from the SK current, as well as the low-voltage-activated calcium channel, are correlated with dAdap. This general principle is supported by datasets from the mouse primary motor cortex and multiple macaque brain regions. Finally, we generate testable predictions by constructing a minimal computational model.

primary.title: Spatial transcriptomics profiling across tissue boundaries in the developing mouse brain.
primary.abstract: Tissue boundaries preserve structural integrity and guide cell differentiation during development, despite constant stress from proliferation, cell death, and tissue deformation. To study gene regulation in these regions we developed REBOSEP, a workflow for analyzing spatial transcriptomics data to detect tissue boundaries and measure gene expression relative to boundary distance. REBOSEP uses hierarchical clustering to uncover shared regulatory patterns among genes, revealing highly diverse expression changes that can shift sharply across just a few cell layers. Using this approach, the study generated the first resource of gene expression across tissue boundaries, covering five brain-meninges boundaries in the developing mouse brain. Analysis of the dorsal pallium-meninges boundary showed specific regulatory patterns in outer brain and meningeal layers, with strong links to developmental processes and distance-dependent regulation in major pathways, including those involved in neurodevelopmental disease and cancer. Overall, REBOSEP provides a systematic framework for studying gene expression regulation at tissue boundaries.

primary.title: Lysosomal multi-omics reveals altered sphingolipid catabolism associated with lysosomal dysfunction in the aging brain.
primary.abstract: Lipids dynamically reside in multiple intracellular locations, and their organellar distribution is important for function. During brain aging, lysosomal lipid changes have been noted, but lipid identity, interactions, and functional relevance have not been characterized. We used mass spectrometry to assess longitudinal changes in the lipidome and proteome of lysosomal fractions from the murine cortex, from 3 to 24 months, followed by multi-omics factor analysis (MOFA) to identify factors underlying lysosomal aging. Our data uncover an age-dependent increase in lysosomal abundance of lipid and protein myelin components and suggest altered sphingolipid catabolism favoring degradation of sphingomyelins over glycosphingolipids. We experimentally corroborate MOFA predictions to demonstrate that age-dependent accumulation of myelin-derived glycosphingolipids is associated with lysosomal enlargement and dysfunction and is most pronounced in microglia. Our findings suggest that age-related lysosomal lipidome changes resemble those observed in lysosomal storage diseases and underscore the importance of organelle-specific analyses for elucidating lipid function.

primary.title: Fer-1 improves cognitive dysfunction in chronic kidney disease through the Sirt2/PGC-1α signaling pathway based on RNA sequencing.
primary.abstract: Ferroptosis is a non-apoptotic form of cell death characterized by cellular accumulation of iron-dependent lipid peroxidation. In recent years, a series of studies have proved that ferroptosis participate in the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Notably, cognitive dysfunction is commonly found in CKD patients and it has been recognized as one of CKD pathological features. However, the character of ferroptosis in CKD related cognitive dysfunction remains unclear. This study aims to verify if ferroptosis participates in the CKD related cognitive dysfunction and the underlying mechanism. Then we use Fer-1 and Erastin to explore the effects of ferroptosis on cognition changes in CKD rat. RNA-seq analysis identified ferroptosis related lipid metabolism was significantly changed in CKD rats and the DEGs played an important role in oligodendrocyte differentiation, which were correlated with cognition ability. Fer-1 ameliorated the ultrastructure of hippocampal CA1 region and rescued the myelin sheath injury in CKD rats. Specifically, Fer-1 increased the density of myelinated axons and upregulated the levels of MBP and SOX10 in hippocampus of CKD rats. Notably, Fer-1 decreased the expression of Sirt2 and the AAV-Sirt2 abrogated the beneficial effects of Fer-1 on ferroptosis and myelin sheath in the hippocampus of CKD rats. This study provides a new strategy for improving cognitive dysfunction in CKD.

primary.title: Identification of new targets for the protection against radiation-induced brain injury through integrated dual-omics analysis.
primary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) is a serious complication of cranial radiotherapy, yet its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify novel therapeutic targets for RIBI through integrated dual-omics analysis. METHODS: A mouse model of RIBI was established using 15 Gy of whole-brain X-ray irradiation. Behavioral tests and histopathological examinations were performed to validate cognitive dysfunction and neuronal damage. Hippocampal tissues were analyzed via transcriptomics and metabolomics to uncover key molecular changes. RESULTS: Transcriptomic analysis identified 29 significantly differentially expressed genes, including upregulated neuroinflammatory genes (Pcsk9, Ifi213) and downregulated neuroprotective factors (Tlx3, Irx1, Irx5), implicating exacerbated neuroinflammatory responses and impaired neurodevelopmental processes. Metabolomic profiling revealed 63 significantly altered metabolites, including elevated DNA oxidative damage markers and depleted branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), suggesting mitochondrial dysfunction and increased oxidative stress. Integrated analysis highlighted correlations among neuroinflammation, DNA damage, and metabolic dysregulation, pointing to a potential interplay between these pathways. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that RIBI pathogenesis involves synergistic interactions between neuroinflammation, DNA damage, and metabolic dysregulation. Targeting Pcsk9, enhancing DNA repair capacity, or supplementing BCAAs could represent potential neuroprotective strategies, although these correlative findings require functional validation. These findings provide a foundation for future studies on mitigating cognitive decline in patients receiving cranial radiotherapy.

primary.title: Chronic Intermittent Hypoxia Induces Hippocampal Cellular Remodeling through microglial polarization imbalance and neural functional disconnection.
primary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment in Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome (OSAHS) is primarily driven by chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH), yet the systemic, dynamic responses of hippocampal cell types to CIH are unclear. METHODS: Using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), we analyzed hippocampal tissues from mice under normoxia or after 2 or 6 weeks of CIH. Integrated analyses assessed cellular composition, pseudotemporal trajectories, intercellular communication, and cell-type-specific responses. RESULTS: CIH induced time-dependent hippocampal reorganization, characterized by a biphasic microglial response (an initial increase followed by a subsequent decline), progressive neuronal loss, and late-stage oligodendrocyte expansion. Pseudotime analysis revealed a coherent cellular transition from a synaptic/functional state, through an adaptive metabolic state, toward a terminal inflammatory state, identifying early-response genes such as Ptgds, S100a8, and S100a9. The intercellular communication network was extensively rewired, marked by strengthened microglia-oligodendrocyte crosstalk yet drastically attenuated neuronal input signals, suggesting functional disconnection of neurons. Mechanistically, microglia were activated via HIF-1 and p53 pathways and exhibited a polarization imbalance toward pro-inflammatory and oxidative-stress phenotypes. Neurons showed enriched pathways for synaptic dysfunction and apoptosis, while oligodendrocytes displayed a signature of maturational arrest involving simultaneous activation of myelination and oxidative-stress programs. CONCLUSION: This study delineates a high-resolution, dynamic map of CIH-induced hippocampal disruption. Our findings suggest that CIH initiates a multicellular pathological program in which microglial polarization imbalance serves as a central regulatory node, linking hypoxia to neural dysfunction. These findings reveal novel cellular mechanisms in OSAHS-related cognitive impairment and highlight candidate pathways for future investigation.

secondary.title: Exploratory chromosome 14-focused transcriptomic profiling of PSEN1-associated familial Alzheimer's disease across brain regions.
secondary.abstract: Familial Alzheimer's disease (FAD) is an inherited form of early-onset Alzheimer's disease associated with pathogenic variants in presenilin 1 (PSEN1). To explore chromosome 14-associated transcriptional patterns in FAD across anatomically distinct brain regions, publicly available RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) datasets from frontal cortex, temporal cortex, and whole-brain samples were analyzed. Because one FAD sample and one control sample were available for each brain region, expression differences were evaluated descriptively using observed log₂ fold-change values rather than conventional inferential differential-expression statistics. Functional annotation and protein-protein interaction analyses were subsequently used to provide biological context for the observed expression patterns. Distinct regional expression patterns were observed within the chromosome 14-focused dataset. Higher expression was observed for representative genes including FITM1, IFI27, AHSA1, and NFKBIA in the frontal cortex, and DHRS4L2, ESR2, GPR65, EFCAB11, and HOMEZ in the temporal cortex. The observed expression patterns were associated with inflammatory, cellular stress, metabolic, receptor-mediated, proteostatic, and neuronal signaling-related functions. Network analysis was used to contextualize these expression patterns rather than to infer causal regulatory relationships. Five representative proteins-NFKBIA, ESR2, GPR65, AHSA1, and IFI27-were further examined structural information to provide structural context for selected transcriptomic observations. Given the absence of biological replication and the chromosome 14-focused design, these findings should be considered descriptive and hypothesis-generating. Independent replicated cohorts and complementary transcriptomic, proteomic, and functional studies are required to determine the reproducibility and biological relevance of the observed patterns.

secondary.title: Feature selection and dimensionality reduction in multi-omics.
secondary.abstract: High-throughput multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional, heterogeneous and noisy datasets, making robust biomarker discovery and disease modelling challenging. This review critically examines dimensionality reduction and representation strategies for multi-omics analysis while distinguishing three related but different goals: feature selection, feature extraction/representation learning, and multi-omics integration. We use sparse canonical correlation analysis (sCCA), variational autoencoders (VAEs), and graph convolutional networks (GCNs) as representative case studies spanning sparse linear, probabilistic deep-learning, and graph-based approaches. Rather than treating these methods as interchangeable, we compare their data requirements, assumptions, interpretability, ability to accommodate non-linearity and missing modalities, computational demands, and validation needs. Applications across cancer, cardiovascular and neurodegenerative disease, and across bulk, single-cell, spatial and imaging multi-omics are summarized in comparative tables. We conclude with practical guidance for matching method families to biological questions and emphasize that robust biomarker claims require leakage-free model development, stability assessment and independent validation.

secondary.title: Thalamic PDK-PDHA1 Signaling is Associated with Opioid-Induced Loss-of-Righting-Reflex Sensitivity: Evidence from Phosphoproteomic Profiling and PDK Pathway Intervention.
secondary.abstract: Opioids are widely used in clinical sedation and anesthesia, but the downstream phosphorylation events associated with opioid-induced reductions in arousal remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether thalamic phosphoproteomic remodeling and the pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase (PDK)-pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 alpha subunit (PDHA1) pathway are associated with opioid-induced loss of righting reflex (LORR) in rats. Phosphoproteomic profiling of rat thalamic tissues after treatment with fentanyl, FENT-001 (a synthetic fentanyl analog), and other sedative and anesthetic agents revealed broad changes in thalamic phosphopeptide abundance.Differentially phosphorylated proteins were enriched in neuronal projections, synapses, cytoskeletal organization and synaptic transmission. PDHA1 was identified as a significantly differentially phosphorylated protein and was further examined by Western blotting. Fentanyl and 3-methylfentanyl altered phosphorylation at multiple PDHA1 sites. Pharmacological inhibition of PDKs with dichloroacetate reduced PDHA1 Ser293 phosphorylation in cultured cortical neurons and produced numerical increases in the estimated ED50 values for fentanyl- and 3-methylfentanyl-induced LORR. These changes were consistent with a trend toward reduced LORR sensitivity. Conversely, CM-targeted overexpression of PDK2 or PDK4 shifted the fitted fentanyl-induced LORR dose-response curves to the left relative to the Vector control, with a larger numerical reduction in ED50 following PDK2 overexpression.These findings suggest that opioid treatment remodels the thalamic phosphoproteome and that the PDK-PDHA1 phosphorylation pathway is functionally associated with opioid-induced LORR sensitivity.

secondary.title: Evaluation of Methylmercury-Induced Motor Dysfunction and Proteomic Analysis of Cerebrospinal Fluid in Common Marmosets (Callithrix jacchus).
secondary.abstract: Methylmercury (MeHg) poisoning can lead to Minamata disease, often manifesting as motor dysfunction. We aimed to establish a quantitative evaluation method for MeHg exposure-associated motor dysfunction in the common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus). Three male marmosets were orally administered MeHg (1.5 mg Hg/kg/day) for 2 weeks, followed by a 2-week non-treatment period; three control marmosets received vehicle. Walking and spontaneous behavior were recorded weekly. After marking body segments, bounding gait videos were analyzed to assess locomotion speed, hip joint position, knee angle, dorsal neck-to-torso angle, and spontaneous behavior. In Hg-1 (MeHg-exposed marmoset with earliest symptom onset), locomotion speed and stride length decreased, while stride time increased. In Hg-2 (second marmoset to exhibit symptom onset), hip joint position and knee angle initially showed relatively normal fluctuations during bounding gait. However, their lower limits decreased following MeHg administration, and the dorsal neck-to-torso angle shifted from negative to positive. Spontaneous activity of Hg-1 and Hg-2 significantly decreased after MeHg administration. These results indicate that MeHg exposure-associated motor dysfunction in marmosets can be detected using our method, with particularly prominent lower-limb abnormalities. Furthermore, cerebrospinal fluid proteomic profiling revealed coordinated disruptions converging on three pathological axes-neuronal injury and neuroprotective responses, neuronal metabolic failure and cytosolic enzyme leakage, and impaired transport and homeostatic regulation-identifying nine proteins as candidate biomarkers. Proteomic alterations were consistent with the observed neuronal injury, neuroinflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and impaired homeostatic regulation in affected motor pathways. These findings establish the marmoset as a translational primate model for neurotoxicological assessments and biomarker discovery.

secondary.title: Single-cell reanalysis characterizes an Osmr+ astrocyte state and predicts midkine signaling to Cox6b1+ glutamatergic neurons at 24 h after traumatic brain injury.
secondary.abstract: BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term neurological disability worldwide. The cellular heterogeneity and intercellular communication in the injured brain remain incompletely defined, particularly astrocyte-neuron crosstalk, which may reveal potential therapeutic targets. METHODS: We reanalyzed the publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset GSE290150, comprising 60,962 high-quality cells from the ipsilateral cortex of mice at 24 h after TBI or sham surgery. Integrated bioinformatic analyses, including unsupervised clustering, gene-set activity scoring, pseudotime inference, transcriptional regulatory network analysis using SCENIC, and cell-cell communication inference using CellChat, were performed to characterize the early post-TBI cellular landscape. RESULTS: We identified five astrocyte subpopulations. Descriptive analysis of the pooled cells showed a greater proportion of C3 Osmr+ astrocytes in the TBI group than in the Sham group. This subpopulation exhibited a highly reactive transcriptional state with concurrent protection-associated and neurotoxicity-associated features, together with relatively high oxidative-phosphorylation- and glutamate-metabolism-related activity scores and elevated inferred Tfe3 regulon activity. Among ten neuronal subpopulations, C0 Cox6b1+ glutamatergic neurons displayed oxidative-phosphorylation- and aerobic-respiration-related features. CellChat analysis prioritized Mdk-Ncl as a candidate ligand-receptor interaction contributing to inferred communication from C3 Osmr+ astrocytes to C0 Cox6b1+ neurons, suggesting a potential astrocyte-to-neuron communication pattern after TBI. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies a TBI-associated C3 Osmr+ astrocyte subpopulation characterized by the highest pan-reactive signature together with protection-associated, neurotoxicity-associated, and metabolic gene expression features, and prioritizes C0 Cox6b1+ glutamatergic neurons as a candidate recipient population of astrocyte-derived MK signaling. Tfe3 was further prioritized as a candidate transcriptional regulator associated with the C3 Osmr+ astrocyte state. These findings provide a valuable framework for advancing experimental studies of astrocyte-neuron communication after TBI.

best.title: Integration of polygenic risk with single cell methylation data using met-scDRS.
best.abstract: MOTIVATION: Although large scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified many risk variants for psychiatric traits their functional implication remain largely unknown. One potential mechanism for their risk is through cellular context-dependent epigenetics such as methylation. Previous methodologies have focused on integrating GWAS with single cell transcriptomics, which allowed identification of within-cell-type heterogeneity in disease risk association. We extended this framework to provide a method called met-scDRS that integrates GWAS with single cell epigenomics and investigates how psychiatric disease risk can manifest through methylomics at single cell resolution. RESULTS: We propose an approach that integrates single cell methylomes with disease associated genes identified from GWAS at single-cell resolution. We found our method to be well calibrated and powered in different scenarios. We then analyzed a publicly available single cell methylome dataset of the human brain for 75 different traits and generated disease relevance scores for each cell for each trait. We find high brain specificity with major cell type enrichments congruent with known findings. We identify within-cell-type heterogeneity for psychiatric disease risk along the brain spatial axis as well as subpopulations that are differentially associated with diseases. Finally, we showed that genes with high correlation between methylation levels and disease relevance scores to be highly enriched in specific functional pathways such as synaptic formation and transmission. AVAILABILITY: met-scDRS is freely available in GitHub as a python package under MIT license: https://github.com/bogdanlab/met-scDRS. Source code is also available from Zenodo with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21841506. All dataset used in this work are publicly available. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

best.title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics uncovers region-specific molecular features underlying selective aging vulnerability of cholinergic neurons.
best.abstract: Cholinergic neurons exhibit functional and molecular heterogeneity across the basal forebrain (BF), midbrain (MB), and brainstem (BS), while the aging-associated transcriptional features remain poorly characterized. Here, we performed single nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on 108,062 nuclei from the MS/VDB, HDB/SI, PPTG/LDTG, 7N, and 12N in adult and aged mice. BF cells showed greater age-associated transcriptomic alterations than MB and BS cells, with pronounced region-specific divergence among cholinergic neurons. Intercellular communication analysis revealed BF-specific age-related changes in APP and ApoE signaling. Within this altered milieu, intrinsic transcriptional responses varied across brain regions. In aged BF cholinergic neurons, transcriptional responses were characterized by increased oxidative stress and inflammatory signatures and reduced expression of genes involved in neuronal structural maintenance. In contrast, MB and BS cholinergic neurons maintained relatively stable transcriptional profiles. These findings reveal region-specific associations between extracellular signaling and intrinsic transcriptional stress, highlighting a selective imbalance that underlies the vulnerability of BF cholinergic neurons.

best.title: Female iPSC X chromosome inactivation erosion and its transcriptomic effects during CRISPR gene editing and neural differentiation.
best.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), together with CRISPR editing, are commonly used for studying neurodevelopmental disorders. Female iPSCs gradually lose the expression of the noncoding X chromosome inactive-specific transcript (XIST), leading to random X chromosome inactivation (XCI) erosion that affects both X-linked and autosomal gene expression. However, the effects of CRISPR editing and neural differentiation on XCI erosion and how this may confound a real-world analysis of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) are poorly understood. Here, we analyzed hundreds of RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) samples of CRISPR-edited iPSC lines for 66 genes and the matched single-neuron RNA-seq data. We found variable XCI in CRISPR-edited female iPSCs, which was largely preserved in iPSC-derived neurons and predominantly influenced X-linked genes. Mechanistically, XIST mediates allele-specific epigenetic regulation of both X-linked and autosomal genes, with the former showing stronger allele-specific expression (ASE) bias that affects neurodevelopmental genes. These results have significant implications in hiPSC-based modeling of neurodevelopmental disorders.

best.title: Single-cell atlas of neuroma-induced DRG remodeling reveals intervention-specific glial and immune programs.
best.abstract: Peripheral nerve injury caused by cut, crush, or excessive stretch can lead to disordered regeneration and painful neuroma formation. Regrowing axons may terminate in a swollen, hypersensitive nerve stump, producing pain that can outweigh sensory or motor deficits. Despite the frequency of neuromas, treatment outcomes remain inconsistent, and the mechanisms that initiate and sustain neuroma-associated pain are poorly understood. A proximal nerve crush performed upstream of a neuroma or transection may reshape axonal growth and interrupt retrograde injury signaling, potentially promoting a regenerative, pain-resolving state. However, its long-term effects on dorsal root ganglion (DRG) programs remain unclear. Here, we use single-cell RNA sequencing to build an atlas of DRG remodeling after neuroma-forming injury and compare it with two interventions: proximal nerve crush and nerve resection. By resolving transcriptional responses across sensory neurons, satellite glial cells, Schwann cells, and macrophages, we identify intervention-specific glial, neuronal, and immune programs that distinguish regenerative from persistent injury-associated states and nominate pathways that may guide mechanism-based therapies for painful neuromas.

best.title: An integrative transcriptomic atlas of ALS and aging skeletal muscle defines shared and distinct molecular programs of degeneration.
best.abstract: Skeletal muscle atrophy and weakness resulting from loss of motor neuron innervation are shared hallmarks of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and age-associated sarcopenia. However, muscle wasting in ALS is rapid and severe, whereas sarcopenia progresses gradually over decades, peaking at an advanced age. The molecular mechanisms underlying muscle wasting in these conditions remain incompletely defined. Here, we used the SOD1G93A ALS mouse model and wild-type mice across the lifespan to generate an integrated single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of skeletal muscle, mapping changes associated with ALS and aging. This atlas is complemented by structural and functional analyses. Our results identify transcriptionally distinct condition-specific myonuclear states, including disease-responsive programs within synaptic myonuclei at the neuromuscular junction, that are shared or distinct between the two conditions. Notably, at early stages, muscle from ALS mice exhibits molecular hallmarks of aged muscle at the myofiber level, indicating premature aging and reinforcing aging as a risk factor in ALS. At advanced disease stages and in old age, myonuclear subpopulations follow similar degenerative pathways in fast glycolytic fibers, consistent with their loss in both conditions. However, a distinct ALS-enriched myonuclei subpopulation displays uniquely regulated genes not observed in aged muscle, potentially underlying the more rapid and severe pathology observed in ALS. This atlas maps shared and divergent mechanisms of muscle degeneration in ALS and sarcopenia and provides a resource for identifying therapeutic targets tailored to each condition.

best.title: Genome-wide CRISPR screen reveals that Wnt signaling regulates lipid accumulation in APOE4 oligodendrocytes.
best.abstract: APOE4 is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease, yet the cellular mechanisms linking APOE variants to disease risk remain unclear. We previously found that APOE4 expression causes lipid droplet accumulation in oligodendrocytes, reducing myelination, but the underlying mechanisms were unknown. Using a genome-wide CRISPR screen and assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (ATAC) sequencing in human-induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived oligodendrocytes, we identified decreased Wnt signaling and overactive glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK3B) as key regulators of lipid-droplet accumulation. Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of GSK3B reduced lipid droplets in APOE4 oligodendrocytes and increased myelination in three-dimensional iPSC-derived brain organoids. Pharmacological GSK3B inhibition also reduced lipid droplets and improved myelination in APOE4;PS19 tau transgenic mice. Together, these findings establish a mechanistic framework linking Wnt/GSK3B signaling to APOE4-driven disruptions in oligodendrocyte lipid metabolism and myelination, pointing to GSK3B as a potential therapeutic target for APOE4-associated Alzheimer's disease.

best.title: Multi-omic profiling of 85 iPSC lines from familial dementia reveals cellular diversity and regulators of organoid development.
best.abstract: Systematic molecular characterization of human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines carrying disease-associated mutations is needed to distinguish disease-related biology from variation in cell state, genomic integrity, and genome-editing history, yet such systematic characterization is uncommon. Here, we profiled 85 human iPSC lines carrying MAPT mutations and isogenic controls using whole-genome sequencing, long-read sequencing of the MAPT locus, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, and DNA methylation arrays. Single-cell analyses identified four reproducible iPSC states and candidate surface markers for their isolation. Whole-genome sequencing revealed unintended editing events and recurrent 20q11.21 duplications, which were associated with increased ID1 expression and impaired cortical organoid patterning. Transcriptomic analyses identified pathways associated with organoid quality and changes linked to clonal selection and editing, underscoring the need to use unconverted lines as isogenic controls. By providing an in-depth genomic characterization of MAPT iPSCs, this dataset serves as a proof of principle to enhance iPSC utility in biological research.

best.title: Early lineage divergence segregates sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus.
best.abstract: The thalamus integrates sensory, motor and associative functions through distinct nuclei, yet the developmental principles driving their specification remain unclear. Here we generate a spatiotemporal single-cell multiomic and spatial transcriptomic atlas of the embryonic mouse thalamus, combined with barcoding-based lineage tracing. We identify two major glutamatergic lineages, sensory-related and motor-associative, each governed by different gene regulatory programs and temporal dynamics. These lineages arise from spatially and molecularly distinct progenitor domains, revealing an early segregation of functional identities. Within the sensory lineage, we resolve branching sensory trajectories leading to first-order visual and somatosensory neurons, both emerging from a shared higher-order-like state. Using in silico predictions and in vivo perturbation, we identify Sp9 as a key regulator of visual thalamic fate. Together, our findings define the molecular architecture and developmental trajectories that underpin thalamic modality specification, providing a framework to understand how functional circuits emerge in the mammalian brain.

best.title: A pathogenic AMPAR mutation disrupts hippocampal synapse maturation and homeostasis.
best.abstract: AMPA receptors (AMPARs) mediate fast excitatory synaptic transmission and are critical for activity-dependent synapse maturation and circuit development. De novo missense mutations in AMPAR subunits are linked to neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), yet how these variants disrupt neuronal function remains unclear. Here, we examine a recurrent pathogenic mutation in the GluA1 subunit (GRIA1 p.A636T) that alters AMPAR function and is associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and intellectual disability (ID). Using GluA1A636T knock-in mice of either sex, we identify impairments in hippocampal-dependent learning and working memory. Quantitative proteomics combined with bulk RNA-seq revealed age-dependent molecular remodeling in mutant hippocampus. Synaptic protein alterations were present in juvenile and adult mice, whereas a pronounced upregulation of mitochondrial and glial-associated proteins emerged more strongly in adulthood. Transcriptomic analyses showed partial concordance and highlighted divergence between RNA and protein regulation. Consistent with these molecular changes, there were increases in markers of oxidative stress in juvenile and adult mutant animals, whereas altered mitochondria morphology emerged selectively in adult mutants. Electrophysiological recordings demonstrated reduced basal excitatory transmission, persistence of silent synapses in adulthood and exaggerated activity-dependent synaptic potentiation, which were associated with reduced spine size consistent with impaired synapse maturation. Together, these findings indicate that a pathogenic AMPAR mutation disrupts developmental synapse maturation with secondary metabolic adaptations emerging over time.Significance Statement Mutations in genes encoding AMPA-type glutamate receptors are increasingly linked to neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism and intellectual disability. However, how these mutations disrupt brain function and development remains poorly understood. Using a mouse model carrying a recurrent disease-associated mutation in the GluA1 AMPA receptor subunit, we show that the presence of this mutant subunit protein impairs the normal maturation of excitatory synapses in the hippocampus. Mutant mice retain immature "silent" synapses into adulthood, exhibit abnormal synaptic plasticity, reduced spine size, and deficits in learning and memory. Molecular analyses reveal age-dependent remodeling of synaptic and mitochondrial proteins, suggesting that metabolic changes arise secondary to disrupted synapse development. These findings clarify how pathogenic AMPA receptor variants alter brain function over time.

best.title: Identification of Succinylation-Related Transcriptional Signatures in Alzheimer's Disease: Integrated Bioinformatics Analysis and Clinical Validation.
best.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder involving mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, proteostasis imbalance, and immune-inflammatory alterations. Protein succinylation is closely linked to mitochondrial metabolic status, but peripheral blood transcriptomic signatures related to succinylation in AD remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to identify peripheral blood transcriptional candidate biomarkers associated with a predefined succinylation-related gene set in AD. The GSE63061 dataset was used as the discovery cohort, and GSE63060 served as an external validation cohort. Differential expression analysis, ssGSEA-derived succinylation scoring, and WGCNA were integrated with a predefined succinylation-related gene set. Candidate biomarkers were then refined through four feature selection approaches: LASSO, random forest, SVM-RFE, and Boruta, and their discriminatory performance was evaluated by ROC analysis, nomogram construction, calibration analysis, decision curve analysis, and SHAP analysis. Functional enrichment, GSVA/GSEA, GeneMANIA, immune-cell signature analysis, and single-cell analyses were used to explore biological relevance and cellular distribution. qRT-PCR was performed using peripheral blood-derived PBMC samples for experimental validation. Five genes, NDUFA1, NDUFS5, RPS27A, AIF1, and PRDX1, were identified as candidate biomarkers associated with a succinylation-related transcriptional signature in AD. These genes were mainly involved in mitochondrial complex I activity, oxidative phosphorylation, ribosomal function, protein homeostasis, redox balance, and immune inflammation. Immune-cell signatures and single-cell analyses further suggested that the signature was associated with T cells, B cells, NK cells, and monocytes/macrophages. qRT-PCR confirmed significant downregulation of all five genes in AD PBMC samples (P < 0.05). These findings suggest that peripheral blood transcriptional signatures associated with succinylation-related genes may provide candidate biomarkers and hypothesis-generating clues for AD.

best.title: Exploratory chromosome 14-focused transcriptomic profiling of PSEN1-associated familial Alzheimer's disease across brain regions.
best.abstract: Familial Alzheimer's disease (FAD) is an inherited form of early-onset Alzheimer's disease associated with pathogenic variants in presenilin 1 (PSEN1). To explore chromosome 14-associated transcriptional patterns in FAD across anatomically distinct brain regions, publicly available RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) datasets from frontal cortex, temporal cortex, and whole-brain samples were analyzed. Because one FAD sample and one control sample were available for each brain region, expression differences were evaluated descriptively using observed log₂ fold-change values rather than conventional inferential differential-expression statistics. Functional annotation and protein-protein interaction analyses were subsequently used to provide biological context for the observed expression patterns. Distinct regional expression patterns were observed within the chromosome 14-focused dataset. Higher expression was observed for representative genes including FITM1, IFI27, AHSA1, and NFKBIA in the frontal cortex, and DHRS4L2, ESR2, GPR65, EFCAB11, and HOMEZ in the temporal cortex. The observed expression patterns were associated with inflammatory, cellular stress, metabolic, receptor-mediated, proteostatic, and neuronal signaling-related functions. Network analysis was used to contextualize these expression patterns rather than to infer causal regulatory relationships. Five representative proteins-NFKBIA, ESR2, GPR65, AHSA1, and IFI27-were further examined structural information to provide structural context for selected transcriptomic observations. Given the absence of biological replication and the chromosome 14-focused design, these findings should be considered descriptive and hypothesis-generating. Independent replicated cohorts and complementary transcriptomic, proteomic, and functional studies are required to determine the reproducibility and biological relevance of the observed patterns.

best.title: Feature selection and dimensionality reduction in multi-omics.
best.abstract: High-throughput multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional, heterogeneous and noisy datasets, making robust biomarker discovery and disease modelling challenging. This review critically examines dimensionality reduction and representation strategies for multi-omics analysis while distinguishing three related but different goals: feature selection, feature extraction/representation learning, and multi-omics integration. We use sparse canonical correlation analysis (sCCA), variational autoencoders (VAEs), and graph convolutional networks (GCNs) as representative case studies spanning sparse linear, probabilistic deep-learning, and graph-based approaches. Rather than treating these methods as interchangeable, we compare their data requirements, assumptions, interpretability, ability to accommodate non-linearity and missing modalities, computational demands, and validation needs. Applications across cancer, cardiovascular and neurodegenerative disease, and across bulk, single-cell, spatial and imaging multi-omics are summarized in comparative tables. We conclude with practical guidance for matching method families to biological questions and emphasize that robust biomarker claims require leakage-free model development, stability assessment and independent validation.

best.title: FOXG1 spatiotemporally orchestrates subtype fate specification and patch/matrix identity of striatal spiny projection neurons.
best.abstract: The striatum consists of three main spiny projection neuron subtypes, direct-pathway neurons (dSPNs), indirect-pathway neurons (iSPNs), and recently identified eccentric striatal neurons (eSPNs) with these SPNs organized into two complementary compartments, the patch and the matrix. However, the cellular basis underlying subtype specification especially that of eSPNs, and mechanisms governing the complementary patterning remain unclear. Here, employing single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) combined with loss-of-function we reveal that eSPNs share more developmental similarities with iSPNs and the transcription factor Foxg1 promotes dSPN and iSPN fates but suppresses eSPN fate in ventral region of the lateral ganglionic eminence lineage. Deletion of Foxg1 in progenitors forces both dSPNs and iSPNs into an eSPN fate. While postmitotic Foxg1 deletion impairs patch/matrix identity and leads to SPN aggregation. We identify FOXG1-driven transcriptional programs and key transcription factors that specify each striatal SPN subtype and patch/matrix identity, and uncover FOXG1 directly regulated cell migration- and cell adhesion-related molecules that control SPN migration. Our findings provide insights into striatal development.

best.title: De novo variants in the essential splicing factor gene SRSF3 cause variable developmental phenotypes.
best.abstract: SRSF3 (SRp20), a member of the serine/arginine-rich protein family of splicing factors, plays a central role in constitutive and alternative splicing. The C-terminal arginine/serine-rich domain of SRSF3 undergoes dynamic phosphorylation cycles that regulate its subcellular localization, protein-protein interactions, and nuclear mRNA export while also indirectly modulating the RNA-binding capability. We report nine individuals with variable developmental phenotypes, including developmental delay and/or mild to moderate intellectual disability as the most consistent feature, and de novo SRSF3 variants. These variants comprise c.181G>C (p.Asp61His) and c.242C>G (p.Ser81Trp), affecting highly conserved residues within the RNA recognition motif, c.330_331del (p.Pro111Serfs∗20), c.402_403del (p.Arg137Ilefs∗16), c.477dup (p.Ser160Valfs∗3), and a recurrent nonsense variant c.445C>T (p.Arg149∗). For c.330_331del, nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) was predicted. Qualitative RT-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) of fibroblasts from this individual demonstrated NMD of SRSF3 transcripts containing the variant. However, overall SRSF3 mRNA and protein levels were comparable to control cells, suggestive of a compensatory mechanism acting in these cells. Comprehensive functional studies of ectopically expressed SRSF3Asp61His, SRSF3Ser81Trp, SRSF3Arg137Ilefs∗16, SRSF3Arg149∗, and SRSF3Ser160Valfs∗3 in HEK293T cells revealed reduced complex formation with polyadenylated RNA as well as intrinsic instability of C-terminally truncated variant proteins, correlating with decreased C-terminal phosphorylation. Complex formation with the nuclear export proteins YTHDC1 and NXF1 was reduced for SRSF3Arg137Ilefs∗16 and SRSF3Arg149∗ and increased for SRSF3Ser81Trp. Additionally, nucleocytoplasmic shuttling, assessed in HeLa cells, was reduced for the C-terminally truncated SRSF3 variant proteins. Together, our data demonstrate distinct functional defects for the disease-associated SRSF3 variants, which may underlie phenotypic variability in affected individuals.

best.title: Parkinson's disease-linked D620N mutation selectively alters the brain-specific protein interactome of VPS35.
best.abstract: Mutations in several genes are known to cause familial forms of Parkinson's disease (PD), including mutations in the vacuolar protein sorting 35 ortholog (VPS35) gene linked to late-onset, autosomal dominant PD. VPS35 encodes a core subunit of the retromer complex which functions in endosomal sorting and recycling. It remains unclear how the pathogenic D620N mutation in VPS35 disrupts retromer function to induce neurodegeneration in PD. Using cell- and rodent-based models expressing D620N VPS35, we performed interactome proteomics to identify alterations underlying the pathogenic effects of D620N VPS35 in PD. Using overexpression of VPS35 variants in HEK-293 T cells, we conducted tandem affinity purification (TAP) or co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) with protein chemical crosslinking to determine the native and non-native protein interactomes of wild-type (WT) and D620N VPS35, respectively. Notably, we can confirm the reduced interaction of D620N VPS35 with components of the WASH complex. Additionally, using a viral-mediated gene transfer model of human D620N VPS35 overexpression in adult rat brain, we identify the first brain-specific protein interactome of VPS35. These overexpression models reveal remarkably similar interaction profiles of WT and D620N VPS35, suggesting that the D620N mutation has a subtle effect on the overall VPS35 protein interactome. We also conducted proteomic analysis of brain tissue from a D620N VPS35 knockin (KI) mouse model that expresses VPS35 at endogenous levels. Using co-IP from hemibrain or striatal extracts of WT and D620N VPS35 KI mice, we reveal a high degree of similarity between the brain interactomes of WT and D620N VPS35, further suggesting a subtle effect of the D620N mutation on VPS35 protein interactions. Notably, in both hemibrain and striatum, we find a selective decrease in the interaction of two known interactors, TBC1D5 and VPS29, with D620N VPS35. We also performed global proteomic analysis of striatal tissue from D620N VPS35 KI mice and reveal a high degree of similarity between WT and D620N, further suggesting a subtle effect of this mutation. Together, our study provides a comprehensive evaluation of the VPS35 protein interactome and reveals a selective effect of the PD-linked D620N mutation in mammalian cells and brain. Our study provides key insight into the mechanisms of retromer dysfunction in VPS35-linked PD.

best.title: Single-cell multiome landscape reveals elovanoid-mediated suppression of inflammatory glial states and induction of homeostatic signaling after ischemic stroke.
best.abstract: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of death and disability. Administration of the lipid mediators elovanoids (ELVs) is protective in human neuronal-glia cultures and in experimental ischemic stroke. We now report using a single-cell multiome approach that intranasally-delivered (IN) ELV34 or its precursor reduced the loss of neuronal markers and upregulated homeostatic microglia signatures after stroke. Thus, ELV reduces disease-associated microglia (expressing Spp1, Gpnmb, Lgals3, Clec7a) and the expression of neuroinflammatory signaling genes. In astrocytes, ELV decreased reactive astrocytes (expressing Gfap, Vim, Nes, Lcn2) and upregulated genes involved in synaptic organization. Also, ELV reduced abundance of oligodendrocytes and OPCs expressing immune markers. ELV induced a phenotype shift from pro-inflammatory microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and OPCs in response to ischemic stroke damage. ELV upregulated gene pathways promoting synaptic integrity, reducing immune cell activation and neuronal loss.

best.title: Patch-seq analysis reveals transcriptomic correlates of neuronal firing rate adaptation across subtypes and species.
best.abstract: Can the transcriptomic profile of a neuron predict its physiological properties? Using a Patch-seq dataset of the primary visual cortex, we addressed this question by focusing on spike rate adaptation (SRA), a well-known phenomenon that depends on small conductance calcium (Ca)-dependent potassium (SK) channels. We first show that in parvalbumin-expressing (PV) and somatostatin-expressing (SST) interneurons, expression levels of genes encoding the ion channels underlying action potential generation are correlated with the half-width (HW) of spikes. Surprisingly, the SK encoding genes are not correlated with the degree of SRA (dAdap). Instead, genes that encode proteins upstream from the SK current, as well as the low-voltage-activated calcium channel, are correlated with dAdap. This general principle is supported by datasets from the mouse primary motor cortex and multiple macaque brain regions. Finally, we generate testable predictions by constructing a minimal computational model.

best.title: Spatial transcriptomics profiling across tissue boundaries in the developing mouse brain.
best.abstract: Tissue boundaries preserve structural integrity and guide cell differentiation during development, despite constant stress from proliferation, cell death, and tissue deformation. To study gene regulation in these regions we developed REBOSEP, a workflow for analyzing spatial transcriptomics data to detect tissue boundaries and measure gene expression relative to boundary distance. REBOSEP uses hierarchical clustering to uncover shared regulatory patterns among genes, revealing highly diverse expression changes that can shift sharply across just a few cell layers. Using this approach, the study generated the first resource of gene expression across tissue boundaries, covering five brain-meninges boundaries in the developing mouse brain. Analysis of the dorsal pallium-meninges boundary showed specific regulatory patterns in outer brain and meningeal layers, with strong links to developmental processes and distance-dependent regulation in major pathways, including those involved in neurodevelopmental disease and cancer. Overall, REBOSEP provides a systematic framework for studying gene expression regulation at tissue boundaries.

best.title: Lysosomal multi-omics reveals altered sphingolipid catabolism associated with lysosomal dysfunction in the aging brain.
best.abstract: Lipids dynamically reside in multiple intracellular locations, and their organellar distribution is important for function. During brain aging, lysosomal lipid changes have been noted, but lipid identity, interactions, and functional relevance have not been characterized. We used mass spectrometry to assess longitudinal changes in the lipidome and proteome of lysosomal fractions from the murine cortex, from 3 to 24 months, followed by multi-omics factor analysis (MOFA) to identify factors underlying lysosomal aging. Our data uncover an age-dependent increase in lysosomal abundance of lipid and protein myelin components and suggest altered sphingolipid catabolism favoring degradation of sphingomyelins over glycosphingolipids. We experimentally corroborate MOFA predictions to demonstrate that age-dependent accumulation of myelin-derived glycosphingolipids is associated with lysosomal enlargement and dysfunction and is most pronounced in microglia. Our findings suggest that age-related lysosomal lipidome changes resemble those observed in lysosomal storage diseases and underscore the importance of organelle-specific analyses for elucidating lipid function.

best.title: Thalamic PDK-PDHA1 Signaling is Associated with Opioid-Induced Loss-of-Righting-Reflex Sensitivity: Evidence from Phosphoproteomic Profiling and PDK Pathway Intervention.
best.abstract: Opioids are widely used in clinical sedation and anesthesia, but the downstream phosphorylation events associated with opioid-induced reductions in arousal remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether thalamic phosphoproteomic remodeling and the pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase (PDK)-pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 alpha subunit (PDHA1) pathway are associated with opioid-induced loss of righting reflex (LORR) in rats. Phosphoproteomic profiling of rat thalamic tissues after treatment with fentanyl, FENT-001 (a synthetic fentanyl analog), and other sedative and anesthetic agents revealed broad changes in thalamic phosphopeptide abundance.Differentially phosphorylated proteins were enriched in neuronal projections, synapses, cytoskeletal organization and synaptic transmission. PDHA1 was identified as a significantly differentially phosphorylated protein and was further examined by Western blotting. Fentanyl and 3-methylfentanyl altered phosphorylation at multiple PDHA1 sites. Pharmacological inhibition of PDKs with dichloroacetate reduced PDHA1 Ser293 phosphorylation in cultured cortical neurons and produced numerical increases in the estimated ED50 values for fentanyl- and 3-methylfentanyl-induced LORR. These changes were consistent with a trend toward reduced LORR sensitivity. Conversely, CM-targeted overexpression of PDK2 or PDK4 shifted the fitted fentanyl-induced LORR dose-response curves to the left relative to the Vector control, with a larger numerical reduction in ED50 following PDK2 overexpression.These findings suggest that opioid treatment remodels the thalamic phosphoproteome and that the PDK-PDHA1 phosphorylation pathway is functionally associated with opioid-induced LORR sensitivity.
